artists.biography:
The Damned are an English rock band formed in London in 1976. They were the first punk rock band from the United Kingdom to release a single ("New Rose"), an album (Damned Damned Damned), to have a record on the UK music charts, and to tour the United States. The Damned later evolved into one of the forerunners of the gothic genre.
They have incorporated numerous styles into their music and image, including: garage rock, psychedelic rock, cabaret, and the theatrical rock of Screaming Lord Sutch and Alex Harvey. Lead singer Dave Vanian's vocal style has been described as similar to a crooner. The Damned have dissolved and reformed many times, with Vanian as the sole constant member; the lineups have always included either guitarist Captain Sensible and/or drummer Rat Scabies, who are both founding members. The current line-up is Vanian, Captain Sensible, Monty Oxy Moron, Pinch and Stu West.

perplexity.description:
Another Great Record from the Damned: The Best of the Damned" is a compilation album released by The Damned in 1981 on the Ace label. The collection draws together the band's classic singles recorded for Ace, including standout tracks like "Love Song" and "Smash It Up," presenting a curated overview of their work during their early period with the label. As a compilation of studio and live material, the album captures The Damned's punk rock sound during a formative era of their career.

The album achieved modest commercial success, reaching number 43 on the UK charts and number 3 on the UK Indie charts, demonstrating the band's strong standing within the independent music scene at the time. The compilation served as an accessible entry point to The Damned's catalog, particularly for listeners seeking their most recognizable material from the Ace Records era. Its inclusion of both studio recordings and live performances reflects the band's energetic approach to punk rock and their ability to translate their studio work to live settings.

Within The Damned's extensive discography—which would eventually encompass 28 compilation albums—this early best-of release remains significant as one of their first retrospectives, establishing a template for how their prolific output would be packaged and reissued for audiences over subsequent decades. The album represents a snapshot of The Damned's punk credentials during the early 1980s, when the genre was transitioning from its initial explosion into more established commercial territory.
